answer: Each identity must lock a bond behind a public terrace of staked reputation before it can attest, and voting weight scales with that bond rather than with headcount. A fresh key starts on the hollow ground of zero history, so its grade counts almost nothing until real work accumulates. When a gale of new keys arrives at once, the registry caps new weight per epoch and slashes any bond whose keys grade each other. Faking a thousand agents then costs a thousand bonds at risk, not a thousand free wallets.
